title: As a developer, I can create an instant copy-on-write branch of my database — schema and data — to develop and test against production-shaped data
As a platform-engineer, I can create and tear down per-pull-request database branches automatically from CI or my deploy platform
As a developer, I can reset a branch from its parent or restore it to an earlier state without rebuilding from a dump
As a developer, I can create a ready-to-connect database in seconds through the CLI or API without capacity planning
As a founder, idle databases scale to zero so prototypes and side projects cost nothing while the data stays durable
As a platform-engineer, compute autoscales up and down with load automatically, without manual resizes or downtime
As a developer, I can query over HTTP or WebSockets from serverless and edge functions with an official driver built for short-lived connections
As a platform-engineer, a built-in connection pooler handles thousands of concurrent connections without me operating my own pgbouncer or proxy
As a developer, I can place data or replicas in regions close to my users to keep read latency low worldwide
As a developer, I can ship schema changes safely — online DDL, deploy requests, or branch-and-merge workflows — without locking or breaking production
As a developer, I can import an existing production database with minimal downtime using a documented migration path
As a developer, the database works out of the box with my ORM and framework (Prisma, Drizzle, Django, Rails) with documented guides
As a platform-engineer, I can restore or branch the database to any point in time within the retention window to recover from bad writes
As a founder, automatic backups run on a schedule I can see and configure, and restores are self-serve
As a platform-engineer, I can add read replicas and rely on documented high-availability and failover behavior
As a developer, I can run the same engine locally and keylessly — no account or cloud dependency — for offline development and CI tests
As a developer, the official CLI covers my daily loop — create, connect, shell into, and inspect databases — without opening the dashboard
As a developer, I can store embeddings and run vector similarity search natively without adding a separate vector database
As a developer, I get real engine compatibility — the Postgres, MySQL, or SQLite dialect and extensions my existing code expects — not a lookalike subset
As a developer, I can run heavy analytical aggregations over large tables fast enough for dashboards without exporting to a separate warehouse
As a platform-engineer, I can see slow queries, index recommendations, and performance metrics in a built-in insights view
As a founder, I can set spend caps or usage alerts so a runaway query or traffic spike cannot produce a surprise bill
As a founder, published per-unit pricing for compute, storage, and traffic lets me predict my bill before committing
As a founder, a genuinely usable free tier lets me run real prototypes before paying

As an AI-native user, my coding agent can provision a database end to end — create it, fetch the connection string, apply schema, and run queries — through the API, CLI, or MCP without touching the dashboard
As an AI-native user, an agent can run SQL and schema operations through scoped tools that distinguish read-only from destructive actions, so I can safely delegate database work
As an AI-native user, I can cheaply create thousands of isolated databases — one per agent, tenant, or preview — and manage the fleet programmatically
